mainTopic: How far forbidden flavor spreads (חלב in roasted meat, a pot's absorbed taste) and who may taste a mixture to check: a כהן, a Jew, or a non-Jewish cook
overview: The גמרא explains why רב הונא forbids a whole kid roasted with its חלב, while a kid roasted with its גיד הנשה may be peeled and eaten: חלב spreads its flavor through the meat. A story in which רבי יוחנן allowed peeling a kid roasted with its fat seems to contradict this. The גמרא answers that the kid was lean. Two other אמוראים tell the story differently: one says it was a kidney with its fat, and the other says it was a small non-kosher fish in a pot, where רבי יוחנן told them to let a non-Jewish cook taste it. רבא then quotes a ברייתא that once troubled him: food cooked in a pot that absorbed meat or תרומה is forbidden only if it gets flavor from the pot. A כהן can taste for תרומה, but who can taste a meat-and-milk mixture? רבא answers with רבי יוחנן's ruling that we rely on a non-Jewish cook. He then begins listing the ways the Sages judge taste, and the list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Forbidden fat spreads its flavor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why רב הונא treats חלב differently from גיד הנשה: חלב spreads its flavor through the whole animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Forbidden fat is different, because its flavor spreads throughout.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why roasting a kid with its חלב makes the whole kid forbidden, while with the גיד הנשה you can peel and eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גיד הנשה gives off only a little flavor, so only the meat close to it is a problem. חלב is fatty and spreads its taste all through the meat, so the whole kid becomes forbidden.

phrases.english: Forbidden fat is different, because it spreads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question on רב הונא's distinction between חלב and גיד הנשה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by how the substance behaves
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think חלב and גיד הנשה should be treated the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: חלב spreads its flavor through the whole animal, so the whole kid is forbidden.

steps.title: A story where רבי יוחנן allowed a kid roasted with its fat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא with a story in which רבי יוחנן allowed peeling and eating a kid that was roasted with its חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really forbidden with its fat? But רבה בר בר חנה said: There was a case before רבי יוחנן in the synagogue of Maon, of a young goat roasted with its fat. They came and asked רבי יוחנן, and he said: Peel and eat until you reach the fat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that seems to show that חלב does not spread through the whole animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוחנן allowed eating the outer meat, then the fat's flavor did not reach everywhere. That goes against the claim that חלב spreads, and against רב הונא's ruling that the kid is forbidden.

phrases.english: And with its fat, it is forbidden?
But didn't Rabba bar bar Chana say:
There was an incident before Rabbi Yochanan
in the synagogue of Maon,
about a young goat that was roasted with its fat,
and they came and asked Rabbi Yochanan,
and he said: One peels and eats
until he reaches its fat!
phrases.notes: So the meat further from the fat was fine, which means the taste did not spread everywhere.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְחֵלֶב אָסוּר? וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer that חלב spreads.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that a kid roasted with its חלב is forbidden, and the reason that חלב spreads
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן allowed the outer meat of a kid roasted with its fat, so the fat's flavor did not spread everywhere.

steps.title: That kid was lean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the kid in רבי יוחנן's case was lean, so its little fat did not spread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains away the story: the kid had very little fat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלב usually spreads, but when there is only a little of it, its flavor does not reach the whole animal. So רבי יוחנן's ruling fits a special case and does not argue with רב הונא.

phrases.english: That one was lean.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the story to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story seemed to prove that the flavor of חלב does not spread through the whole kid.
steps.terutzMaskana: A lean kid has too little fat for the flavor to spread, so peeling is enough.

steps.title: The story was about a kidney with its fat
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה gives a different version: the story was about a kidney roasted with its fat, and רבי יוחנן allowed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said: It was a kidney with its fat, and he permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא says the story was not about a whole kid at all, but about a kidney cooked with its fat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives a second way to remove the challenge. If the case was only a kidney, it tells us nothing about a whole kid roasted with its fat, so רב הונא's ruling stands.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda said:
It was a kidney with its fat, and he permitted it.
phrases.notes: He is telling us what really happened in רבי יוחנן's case, so it is not about a whole kid.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אָמַר: כּוּלְיָא בְּחֶלְבָּהּ הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of the story instead of the 'lean kid' answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case in the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story was about a whole kid roasted with its fat.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was a kidney with its fat, so it does not contradict רב הונא.

steps.title: The story was about a small fish in a pot
steps.stepSummary: רבין בר רב אדא gives a third version: the case was a small non-kosher fish that fell into a pot, and רבי יוחנן said a non-Jewish cook should taste it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר רב אדא said: It was a כילכית fish in a pot. They came and asked רבי יוחנן, and he told them: Let a non-Jewish cook taste it.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא says the story was really about a forbidden fish in a pot of food, not about fat at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רבי יוחנן's ruling depends on taste: if the fish's flavor can be tasted, the food is forbidden. Since the story is not about חלב, it cannot challenge רב הונא.

phrases.english: Ravin bar Rav Adda said:
It was a kilkhit fish in a stewpot,
phrases.notes: A כילכית is a tiny non-kosher fish that fell into the food.

phrases.english: and they came and asked Rabbi Yochanan,
and he said to them: Let a non-Jewish cook taste it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא אָמַר: כִּילְכִּית בְּאִילְפָּס הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third version of the story, different from both earlier answers.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case in the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story was about a kid roasted with its fat.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was about a forbidden fish in a pot, decided by tasting, so it has nothing to do with חלב.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's rule stands: a kid roasted with its חלב is forbidden because חלב spreads. רבי יוחנן's story is explained as a lean kid, a kidney, or a fish in a pot.

steps.title: רבא's early difficulty with a ברייתא about pots
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא that once troubled him: a pot used for meat or for תרומה, and the rule if milk or regular food was cooked in it afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: At first this ברייתא was hard for me: A pot in which meat was cooked, one should not cook milk in it, and if he did, it depends on whether it gives flavor. A pot of תרומה, one should not cook regular food in it, and if he did, it depends on whether it gives flavor.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins a new topic by quoting a ברייתא. He is setting up a difficulty he once had, which the גמרא explains next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that ahead of time you should not use such a pot, but after the fact the food is forbidden only if the absorbed meat or תרומה gives flavor. רבא has not yet said what bothered him. That comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives flavor: the measure for whether the mixture is forbidden
The portion given to a כהן, which regular people may not eat

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: מֵרֵישׁ הֲוָה קָא קַשְׁיָא לִי
phrases.english: Rava said: At first it was difficult for me,
that which was taught in a baraita:
A pot in which one cooked meat –
one should not cook milk in it,
and if he did cook it – it depends on whether it gives flavor;
phrases.notes: The meat soaked into the pot's walls. The milk is forbidden only if that meat gives it a taste.

phrases.english: teruma – one should not cook regular food in it,
phrases.notes: He means a pot in which תרומה was cooked.

phrases.english: and if he did cook it – it depends on whether it gives flavor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מֵרֵישׁ הֲוָה קָא קַשְׁיָא לִי הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts רבא's discussion of a ברייתא about pots. The גמרא brings it here because רבא's difficulty is later solved by רבי יוחנן's ruling in Step 5, in רבין בר רב אדא's version, that we rely on a non-Jewish cook to taste.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pot that absorbed meat or תרומה should not be used for milk or regular food. After the fact, the food is forbidden only if it gets flavor from what the pot absorbed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא shows that flavor absorbed into a pot's walls can forbid food cooked in it later, but only when that flavor is actually given to the new food.

steps.title: Who can taste a meat-and-milk mixture?
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains his difficulty with the ברייתא. A כהן can taste for תרומה, but nobody can taste for בשר בחלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for תרומה, because a כהן can taste it. But for meat in milk, who can taste it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tells us exactly what bothered him about the ברייתא from Step 6. Its rule depends on someone tasting the food, and for meat and milk no one seems able to do that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the food is forbidden only if the earlier food gave it a taste. With תרומה, a כהן is allowed to eat it, so he can taste and report. With בשר בחלב, the mixture might be forbidden to every Jew, so no Jew may taste it, and the rule seems impossible to carry out.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (the גמרא accepts one side before raising a difficulty about the other)
A priest, who is allowed to eat תְּרוּמָה
Meat cooked with milk, which is forbidden to every Jew

phrases.english: Granted, in the case of תרומה,
phrases.notes: This refers to the ברייתא's case of plain food cooked in a pot that was used for תרומה.

phrases.english: a כהן can taste it,
but meat in milk,
who can taste it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא תְּרוּמָה, טָעֵים לַהּ כֹּהֵן, אֶלָּא בָּשָׂר בְּחָלָב – מַאן טָעֵים לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what difficulty רבא had with the ברייתא he quoted in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that a meat pot makes milk forbidden only if it gives a taste
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A taste test needs someone to taste. No Jew may taste a mixture that might be בשר בחלב, so the test seems impossible.

steps.title: We rely on a non-Jewish cook
steps.stepSummary: רבא solves his difficulty using רבי יוחנן's ruling that we rely on a non-Jewish cook to taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that רבי יוחנן said we rely on a non-Jewish cook, here too we rely on a non-Jewish cook.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question. Since רבי יוחנן already said a non-Jewish cook can taste for us, the same method works for meat and milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5, רבי יוחנן said a non-Jewish cook may taste a pot that a small non-kosher fish fell into. רבא applies the same idea here: the cook tastes the milk dish and tells us whether it tastes of meat. So the ברייתא's rule can be carried out after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that (a known ruling settles our question)

steps.whatToRemember: When no Jew can taste a mixture, we rely on a non-Jewish cook to tell us whether the forbidden taste is there. This comes from רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Now that רבי יוחנן said:
phrases.notes: He means רבי יוחנן's ruling about the small non-kosher fish in Step 5.

phrases.english: we rely on a non-Jewish cook,
here too we rely on a non-Jewish cook.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: סָמְכִינַן אַקַּפִּילָא אֲרַמָּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying an established ruling (רבי יוחנן's) to a new case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The meat-and-milk taste test seemed impossible because no Jew may taste it.
steps.terutzMaskana: A non-Jewish cook tastes and reports, just as in רבי יוחנן's fish case.

steps.title: רבא begins a list of ways to measure taste
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens a list: sometimes the Sages rely on a Jew tasting, and sometimes on a non-Jewish cook.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבא said: the Sages spoke about tasting, and the Sages spoke about a cook.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a summary of the different ways the Sages decide whether a taste spread into food. This is a setup line, and the rest of his list continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we have seen two methods. A Jew tastes when he is allowed to, like a כהן with תרומה, and a non-Jewish cook tastes when no Jew may. רבא now lists these methods side by side, and more categories will follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Tasting, here meaning a Jew who is allowed to eat the food tastes it
By a cook, meaning we rely on a non-Jewish cook to taste

phrases.english: For רבא said:
the Sages spoke of relying on tasting,
phrases.notes: He means a Jew who is allowed to eat the food tastes it, like the כהן with תרומה.

phrases.english: and the Sages spoke of relying on a cook,

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רָבָא: אֲמוּר רַבָּנַן בְּטַעְמָא, וַאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן בְּקַפִּילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After using two tasting methods (a כהן and a non-Jewish cook), רבא starts a general list of the ways the Sages judge taste.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are different ways to judge taste: sometimes a permitted Jew tastes, and sometimes we rely on a non-Jewish cook. The list continues.
